title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
statement: You may choose one contiguous block of `nums` and sort only that block into non-decreasing order, leaving every other element where it is. Find the shortest block for which this makes the entire array non-decreasing, and return its length. When `nums` is already non-decreasing the answer is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Sorting a copy and comparing it with `nums` gives the answer in O(n log n): the block runs from the first to the last position where the two differ. To do it in O(n), ask which positions are already final. A value is out of place on the right side of the block exactly when some earlier value is bigger than it; it is out of place on the left side exactly when some later value is smaller than it. A pointer walking in from each end can test this with a running maximum and a running minimum.

## Approach

1. Keep `maxFromLeft` (largest value seen walking right) and `minFromRight` (smallest value seen walking left). Start with `start = 0` and `end = -1` so a sorted array gives `end - start + 1 = 0`.
2. Move `left` from the front and `right = n - 1 - left` from the back in the same loop.
3. If `nums[left]` is below `maxFromLeft`, a bigger value sits before it, so the block must reach at least `left`: set `end = left`.
4. If `nums[right]` is above `minFromRight`, a smaller value sits after it, so the block must start at `right` or earlier: set `start = right`.
5. The last `end` and the last `start` recorded are the block's edges; return `end - start + 1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 6, 4, 8, 10, 9, 15]`. Walking right, the maximum climbs 2, 6, 6, 8, 10, 10, 15; the values 4 (index 2) and 9 (index 5) fall below it, so `end` ends at 5. Walking left, the minimum falls 15, 9, 9, 8, 4, 4, 2; the values 10 (index 4) and 6 (index 1) rise above it, so `start` ends at 1. The answer is `5 - 1 + 1 = 5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one loop with constant work per step.
- Space: O(1): four numbers besides the loop index.

## Pitfalls

- Use strict comparisons: equal values are allowed side by side, so `[3, 3]` needs no sorting.
- Do not stop at the first descent: in `[1, 3, 2, 2, 2]` every 2 is below the earlier 3, so the block runs to the last index.
- Pick `start` and `end` so that an already sorted array returns `0`, not `1` or a negative number.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `left`, `right` | pointers walking in from the front and the back |
| `maxFromLeft` | largest value in `nums[0..left]` |
| `minFromRight` | smallest value in `nums[right..n-1]` |
| `start`, `end` | first and last index of the block that must be sorted |
